text: Wizard: Theurgy

Many gods claim arcane magic as their domain, due to its
nature. Magic is a living, breathing being, as much a part of
the world as any other primordial force. Just as there are
deities of the hunt, the sun and war, the arcane is a domain
under the jurisdiction of many divine patrons.

Many such divine beings grant their blessings to clerics of
their faith, but often also bid their followers to study wizardry
and arcane spellcraft. Such a dedicated user of magic might
find themselves following the arcane tradition of Theurgy.
Arcane Domain

2nd-level Theurgy feature
When you choose this tradition, choose a domain from
your chosen deity's list of eligible domains. Your studies on
elements of divine magic grant you access to certain benefits
depending on your chosen domain, as described in your class
features.

In addition, you learn to speak, read, and write Celestial,
you gain proficiency with the Religion skill and you can use a
holy symbol as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells.
Theurgy Savant

2nd-level Theurgy feature
Whenever you gain a wizard level, you can replace one of
the wizard spells you add to your spellbook with a cleric
domain spell from your chosen domain. The spell must be of
a level for which you have spell slots.

If you add all of your domain spells to your spellbook, you
can subsequently add any spell from the cleric spell list to
your spellbook instead. The spell must still be of a level for
which you have spell slots.

Any cleric spell you gain from this feature is considered a
wizard spell for you, but other wizards can’t copy cleric spells
from your spellbook into their own spellbooks unless they
have also chosen this tradition. Furthermore, due to the
dichotomy between the nature of arcane and divine magic,
you can't choose cleric spells you gain from this feature with
your Spell Mastery and Signature Spell features, which you
gain when you reach higher levels in this class.
Domain Surge

6th-level Theurgy feature
Your understanding over the principles governing your
chosen domain has granted you a pool of excess magic. You
have a pool of domain surges that you use to empower your
domain spells. The number of domain surges in the pool
equals 1 + your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1) .

When you cast a cleric domain spell from your chosen
domain by expending a spell slot, you can expend any
number of domain surges from the pool to increase the
spell's level by an amount equal to the domain surges you
expended, without expending a higher level spell slot. You can
increase a spell's level this way up to the highest level for
which you have spell slots, but no higher than 5th level.

Your pool regains all expended domain surges when you
finish a long rest. As a bonus action, you can expend a spell
slot to regain a number of expended domain surges equal to
the slot's level.
Consecrated Arcana

10th-level Theurgy feature
Your magic is weaved by both arcane and divine energy.
You gain the following benefits

Whenever you cast a wizard spell that deals acid, cold, fire,
lightning, poison or thunder damage, you can change the
type of damage it deals to radiant. If you do, you can add
your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of the spell.
Whenever you cast a wizard spell of 1st level or higher
that restores hit points to a creature, the creature regains
additional hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier (a
minimum of 1 additional hit point) .
Exalted Arcanist

14th-level Theurgy feature
You can harness divine magic to perform miraculous feats
of spellcraft. As an action, you can expend one or more
domain surges from your pool and name a cleric spell of your
choice that is of a level equal to the number of domain surges
you expended and has a casting time of 1 action . You don't
need to meet any requirements of the spell, including any
costly components: the spell simply takes effect as part of this
action.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you
finish a long rest.
